definition: A saturated hydrocarbon whose molecules contain only carbon-carbon and carbon-hydrogen single bonds. The simplest homologous series, with general formula CnH2n+2.
A compound that contains carbon and hydrogen only. The word only is load-bearing: a third element such as oxygen disqualifies the compound.
msAccepts: compound of carbon and hydrogen only
made of just carbon and hydrogen
msAvoids: saying contains carbon and hydrogen without exclusivity

definition: A hydrocarbon with only single bonds between its atoms — no double (C=C) or triple (C≡C) bonds anywhere in the molecule. Alkanes are the saturated family.
msAccepts: no C=C or C≡C double or triple bonds
maximum hydrogen for the carbon count
msAvoids: saying full of hydrogen instead of bonding language
confusing saturation with low reactivity meaning no reactions

definition: One algebraic expression that gives the molecular formula of every member of a homologous series. For alkanes it is CnH2n+2: n carbons carry 2n + 2 hydrogens.
msAccepts: one formula describing all family members
hydrogens equal twice the carbons plus two
msAvoids: mixing up n with a fixed atom count

definition: A series of compounds with the same functional group, similar chemical properties, a trend (gradation) in physical properties, one general formula, and consecutive members differing by a -CH2- unit.
msAccepts: similar chemical properties because same functional group
msAvoids: listing the bullets as unrelated facts
confusing the series with a periodic-table group

definition: The atom or bond arrangement that gives an organic family its characteristic reactions. Alkanes have no reactive group beyond their C-C and C-H single-bond skeleton.
msAccepts: the reactive part of the molecule
alkanes lack one beyond the single-bond skeleton
msAvoids: saying alkanes have a C=C functional group
confusing it with the whole molecule

definition: A compound with the same molecular formula as another compound but a different structural formula. Butane and pentane have branched-chain isomers; methane, ethane and propane have none.
msAccepts: same molecular formula different structural formula

definition: A formula that counts the atoms of each element in one molecule — C3H8 says 3 carbons and 8 hydrogens — without showing how they are joined.
msAccepts: shows what but not how joined
msAvoids: confusing it with the displayed formula

definition: A formula that shows the order in which atoms are joined along the chain — CH3CH2CH3 for propane — without drawing every bond as a line.
msAccepts: shows atom order in the chain
chain order without full bond drawing
msAvoids: confusing it with the molecular formula
saying it shows every bond as a line

definition: A drawing that shows every atom and every covalent bond as an explicit line, including all hydrogen atoms. Each carbon shows exactly four bonds.
msAccepts: every atom and every bond drawn
all C-H bonds shown as lines
msAvoids: leaving a carbon with fewer or more than four bonds
confusing it with the structural formula

definition: A carbon chain in which every carbon sits at an end or in the running line of the chain, with no carbon attached to the middle of another. Also called a straight chain.
msAccepts: no carbon branches off the middle
all carbons in one continuous line
msAvoids: saying the chain is literally straight

definition: The temperature at which a liquid's vapour pressure equals atmospheric pressure and the liquid boils. For alkanes it rises regularly as molecule size increases.
msAccepts: temperature at which a liquid boils
increases with molecule size for alkanes

definition: Forces of attraction between neighbouring molecules. They strengthen as alkane molecules get bigger, which is why larger members boil higher and solids appear at about C18H38.
msAccepts: more energy needed to overcome them
msAvoids: confusing them with covalent bonds inside molecules
saying covalent bonds break on boiling

definition: Burning in a plentiful supply of oxygen, giving carbon dioxide and water only — for example CH4 + 2O2 giving CO2 + 2H2O.
msAvoids: listing carbon monoxide as a complete-combustion product

definition: Burning when oxygen is insufficient: carbon monoxide and/or carbon (soot) form instead of some or all of the carbon dioxide, with water still produced.
A colourless, odourless, toxic gas (CO) formed in incomplete combustion. It reduces the blood's capacity to carry oxygen, which is why it is dangerous to humans.
msAvoids: saying it smells or is visible

definition: Carbon in the form of black particles, deposited when a hydrocarbon burns in severely insufficient oxygen — the carbon that never reached any oxide.
msAccepts: carbon formed in very limited oxygen
appears when oxygen is most scarce

definition: A reaction in which one atom (or group) is replaced by another. Alkanes undergo substitution with halogens in the presence of ultraviolet radiation.
The electromagnetic radiation (UV light) that supplies the energy alkanes' halogen substitution needs — sunlight is the everyday source. Without it the halogen stays as molecules.
msAccepts: provides energy to split halogen molecules
msAvoids: substituting heat or a catalyst as the condition

definition: A substitution product of an alkane and a halogen, named in the format x-haloalkane, where x gives the position of the halogen atom on the longest carbon chain — for example 1-bromopropane and 2-bromopropane.
msAccepts: alkane with a halogen atom replacing a hydrogen
msAvoids: calling it a halogenated addition product

definition: Substitution in which only one hydrogen atom of the alkane is replaced by a halogen atom. Even mono-substitution of propane yields two isomeric products.
msAccepts: propane gives two isomeric monosubstitution products
msAvoids: saying it means one product only

definition: An atom or species with an unpaired electron, formed when UV light splits a halogen molecule. Free radicals are very reactive and attack the otherwise unreactive alkanes.
msAccepts: formed when UV splits halogen molecules
msAvoids: saying free electrons (delocalised electrons is the bonding term)

definition: The gaseous fossil fuel whose major component is methane, with smaller quantities of ethane and propane. Burned for heating and cooking.
msAccepts: contains ethane and propane in small quantities

definition: LPG: a fuel mixture of propane and other small alkanes, stored as liquid under pressure, obtained as a constituent of crude oil distillation.
msAvoids: saying it contains methane as major component
